newsitem.title: JAPAN: Hashimoto, Clinton discuss Russia summit-report.
newsitem.headline: Hashimoto, Clinton discuss Russia summit-report.

text.p: Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto and U.S. President Bill Clinton exchanged views on Russia before Clinton's Helsinki meeting with Russian President Boris Yeltsin on Thursday, media reports said.
In the 20-minute telephone discussion, Clinton told Hashimoto he looked forward to discussing security issues with Yeltsin, the Kyodo news agency said.
"I hope the talks will contribute to security in Europe," Kyodo quoted Clinton as telling Hashimoto. "I will also pledge continued support for President Yeltsin's reform policies."
Clinton and Yeltsin were to meet in the Finnish capital for two days of talks which have already been clouded over by the proposed expansion of NATO.
Hashimoto told Clinton Japan also supports Yeltsin's reforms and asked Clinton to convey to Yeltsin his government's desire for an accelerated political dialogue with Moscow, Kyodo said.
Officials of the Prime Minister's Office were not available for comment on Thursday, a national holiday in Japan.
Hashimoto is scheduled to hold formal talks with Clinton in late April during his visit to Washington.
